name: so

phase_0.boundary_condition: The utterance or sentence that contains the token 'so' as a complete semantic unit.

VINIT.chosen_element: unarticulated intention or proposition before any linguistic encoding
VINIT.justification: void state — no word uttered yet; the raw thought prior to 'so'.

TANCH.justification: terminal anchor that closes the linguistic scope containing 'so'.

AFWD.chosen_element: result or consequence (forward direction from cause to effect)
AFWD.justification: forward morphism from the cause clause to the result clause in a 'so that' construction.

AREV.chosen_element: purpose or intention (reverse direction from effect back to cause)
AREV.justification: reverse morphism indicating the intended outcome that licenses the action.

CLINK.chosen_element: sequential linking of clauses within a compound or complex sentence
CLINK.justification: composition of clauses via 'so' creates a chained relationship.

IMSCRIB.chosen_element: self-reference of the proposition that 'so' stands for (e.g., 'I think so')
IMSCRIB.justification: identity — 'so' refers back to itself or to the preceding discourse; satisfies idempotent self-pointing.

FSPLIT.chosen_element: the conjunction 'so' splitting a sentence into two halfs: the cause/condition and the purpose/result
FSPLIT.justification: splits a unit clause into its constituent propositions: Arm A (the given condition) and Arm B (the intended or actual result).

FFUSE.chosen_element: the same conjunction 'so' fusing the two halves back into a single statement
FFUSE.justification: reconstitutes the original complex sentence from its split parts, preserving the semantic relation introduced by 'so'.

EVALT.chosen_element: affirmative evaluation: the intended result actually occurs (actualization)
EVALT.justification: success state — the purpose is achieved; the outcome matches the intention.

EVALF.chosen_element: negative evaluation: the intended result fails to occur (frustration)
EVALF.justification: failure state — the purpose is not realized; the outcome contradicts the intention.

ENGAGR.chosen_element: both actual and intended outcomes held simultaneously (e.g., counterfactual 'even so' or dialetheic 'so and not so')
ENGAGR.justification: paradice — both arms coexist without resolution, typical of paradoxical self-reference (e.g., 'this sentence is false' using 'so').

IFIX.chosen_element: the permanent record of the utterance (e.g., written sentence, inscription)
IFIX.justification: irreversible fixation of the linguistic act — once said or written, cannot be unsaid.

phase_2.split_element: the conjunction 'so' as a splitter of clauses
phase_2.split_input: a single clause expressing a cause or intention
phase_2.fuse_element: the same conjunction 'so' as a fuse of clauses
phase_2.fuse_result: the original cause clause joined to the result clause via 'so' — semantically identical to the unsplit complex sentence

phase_3.void_description: no proposition expressed; silence or null discourse
phase_3.true_description: the result clause holds as actual (affirmative truth) — register value 01
phase_3.false_description: the result clause does not hold (falsified purpose) — register value 10
phase_3.both_description: the result clause and its negation both hold (paradoxical self-reference via 'so') — register value 11

steps.domain_action: raw intentional state before any linguistic encoding
self-reference — the word 'so' as a placeholding token of the proposition
'so' splits the proposition into cause (Arm A) and result (Arm B)
forward morphism from cause to intended result (Arm A → Arm B)
evaluate if result actually occurs (Arm B truth check)
evaluate if result fails (Arm B false check)
compose the two arms back via the conjunction 'so'
fuse cause and result into a single complex sentence 'cause so result'
inscribe the sentence as a permanent record

phase_5.compiler_frontend: syntax parser that transforms conceptual relations into linearized clause structure
phase_5.ipc_mechanism: rhetorical relation linking (cause/result) between clauses in the discourse
phase_5.memory_mechanism: working memory that holds the prior clause and tracks the anaphoric referent of 'so'
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: discourse planning module that orders main and subordinate clauses
phase_5.alfs_store: the canonical linguistic reference for 'so' as defined in the CL8NK dictionary (PHI_C criticality)

phase_6.cycle_cost: one act of linguistic articulation (phonetic or orthographic production)
phase_6.post_cycle_state: structured, linearized sentence with fixed meaning (reduced entropy due to ordering)
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — the information content is preserved; the cycle merely recodes intention into utterance without loss.
